Track over 50 blood markers across key health areas
25+ markers from wearables, physical tests, and more
Lipids are the fats and cholesterol your body uses to build cells and store energy. Their balance is a strong predictor of long-term heart and blood vessel health.
Your average blood sugar over recent months is a core measure of metabolic health. Persistently raised levels are an early signal of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes risk.
Your kidneys filter waste, balance fluids, and help regulate your blood pressure around the clock. These markers can flag changes before symptoms show up.
Sex hormones shape your energy, mood, libido, and muscle and bone strength. Tracking them gives context for changes you can feel but can't always explain.
Micronutrients are the vitamins, minerals, and fatty acids your body needs daily but can't make itself. Even small shortfalls can drain your energy, immunity, and focus.
Your liver handles hundreds of jobs, from processing food and drink to clearing out toxins. These markers show how well it's coping with the workload.
Your thyroid sets the pace your body runs at — affecting energy, weight, mood, and temperature. Small imbalances can leave you feeling flat, foggy, or out of sync.
Inflammation is your immune system at work. Short bursts protect you, but low-level chronic inflammation is linked to long-term disease — and this is your clearest window into it.
